conviction_note: The one real finding is that management reaffirmed the FY26 outlook on 2026-09-09, nine days after Q3 closed (Aug 31), and said Consumer shipments matched improving consumption. That makes a guide cut, the downside tail the 7.4% implied move and +6.75 put skew are paying for, unlikely. Against it: the reaffirm is public, the Flavor Solutions volume reset was disclosed at the same event, and packaged-food peers sold beat-plus-reaffirm prints this month (CAG -4% on a 46% EPS beat today). So the +0.8 finding is emitted at +0.4, half the sum, because the reaction function and the skew both argue for less.
bar: Q3 revenue ~$1.98B and adj EPS $0.76 (11 analysts, range $0.73-0.80, https://news.alphastreet.com/mccormick-company-mkc-q3-2026-preview-eps-est-0-76-reports-october-1/), which agrees with Zacks $0.75 on ~$2.0B (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:f419653ff094b:0-mccormick-readies-for-q3-earnings-what-to-expect-from-mkc-stock/). Both are consistent with the company's own Q3 guide from the Q2 call: adj operating income up high-single to low-double digits on a $294m base, with a 24% vs 16% tax-rate headwind (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-mccormick-tops-q2-2026-estimates-as-shares-rise-premarket-93CH-4760779). FY26 guide: adj EPS $3.05-3.13, organic +1-3%, reaffirmed 2026-09-09. The bar is sourced, so no cap applied.
positioning_check: MarketBeat, settlement 2026-09-15: 15.95m shares short, 6.64% of float, 5.7 days to cover, -0.6% vs prior report (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MKC/short-interest/). The sweep's fintel snippet reads 3.15% / 7.97 days. Either way this is moderate, not a crowded short. findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-09, nine days after fiscal Q3 closed on Aug 31, management said 'We remain confident in our full-year 2026 outlook' and that Consumer shipments 'broadly matched the improvement seen in consumption trends'. That effectively rules out a guide cut at this print, which is the tail the option market is paying for. The same remarks reset Flavor Solutions to price-driven growth with flattish volume and flagged QSR softness, so the upside is a relief move, not a beat-driven rerating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what moves this stock. Beat plus reaffirm on 2026-06-25 drew +1.58%. The FY26 guide in Jan 2026 drew -8.05%. 'Lowers profit view despite beat' in Oct 2025 drew -3.91%. The Mar 2026 -6.11% was the Unilever deal announcement, not the guide. Peer reaction this month to beat plus reaffirm: CAG -4% on 2026-09-30, GIS roughly flat on 2026-09-23.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market treated the post-quarter reaffirm as binding, the event-implied move would sit near the name's 3.9% median reaction rather than 7.38%, and the 25-delta skew would not be +6.75 vol points into a print whose guide is already known. Instead the stock fell about 9% after the remarks ($51.90 on 09-08 to $47.21), driven by the TD Cowen downgrade, Unilever-deal execution worries and the packaged-food selloff, none of which is a Q3 or FY26 guidance fact. This lands inside what the company already guided to, so it is a firmness call, not a surprise. That is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: UBS preview headline 2026-09-24, 'McCormick Likely to Keep Guidance at Fiscal Q3 Results' (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/mccormick-likely-to-keep-guidance-at-fiscal-q3-results-ubs-says-ce785aded080f522). Different source, same direction, and it also shows the sell side expects a reaffirm, which limits how unpriced this is.

outside_window.finding: Unilever Foods combination: S-4 and proxy not yet filed, close targeted for mid-2027. Scrutiny of reduced social guarantees for non-European Unilever staff (2026-09-16) and the EY-to-KPMG auditor switch (8-K 2026-09-28, deal-driven independence, no disagreements) are deal-timeline items. None resolves inside the window unless it is mentioned on the call. Sized 0.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 8-Ks since Q2: 2026-09-28 item 4.01 is EY dismissed for post-deal independence, KPMG appointed, no disagreements or reportable events (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63754/000006375426000322/mkc-20260924.htm). 2026-08-28 item 5.02 is the audit chair leaving to become Best Buy CFO (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63754/000006375426000305/mkc-20260825.htm). Both benign.
Form 4s in September are phantom-stock plan accruals (Foley, Tapiero), not open-market buying or selling (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000063754/000006375426000317/form4.xml).

Q2 10-Q: no IEEPA refund claim beyond the ~$30.8m already guided ($28m in Q2, ~$3m in H2), no new contingencies. Interest expense is up on bridge and term-loan costs that were already in the June guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000063754/000006375426000274/mkc-20260531.htm).

Tariffs: Section 122 expired 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same day by 10%/12.5% Section 301 forced-labour tariffs. No evidence found that spices are exempt, so this is not an H2 cost tailwind (https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/25037-ag-groups-react-favorably-to-section-301-tariff-exemptions).

Input costs: Vietnam black pepper export price about $6,100/t in mid-September and stable (https://www.vietnam.vn/en/gia-tieu-hom-nay-21-9-my-trung-quoc-tang-nhap-khau-tieu-viet-nam-trong-nua-dau-thang-9). Drewry WCI $4,468 on 09-24, flat to down but with Middle East lanes rising (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-24-september-2026). No clear signal either way.
Spice-category scanner data (Circana/Nielsen) for Jun-Aug 2026: not publicly retrievable.
Recall search: the Perfect Pinch salmonella recall that surfaces is an old story, not 2026.

Unilever deal synergy detail promised for end of September: largely delivered at Barclays on 09-09 ($600m net, about two-thirds by year two, split by source) (https://www.thebanner.com/economy/mccormick-roadmaps-unilever-foods-merger-NET6JZZNV5ABPLG3QOQMHQUY3Y/). No pending disclosure left to surprise.
baseline_tension: The finding cuts against the +6.75 put skew and the -13% 20-day run-up. The option market prices a 7.4% move with downside paid, while the post-quarter reaffirm says the guide tail is mostly closed. But the drawdown is driven by the deal and the sector, not the print, and packaged-food peers are selling reaffirmed beats, so most of what the price holds is not something this print can fix.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6: the reaffirm lands inside what the company already guided to, and UBS publicly expects it. It is a firmness call the market was told to expect, so the finding is cut from +1.5 to +0.8.
Lesson 7: the + sign runs against a +6.75 put skew. The explicit reason (a guide cut is foreclosed by a post-quarter-close reaffirm) is kept, but the size is shrunk as the rule requires.

Lessons 1 and 3: the reaction function (MKC +1.58% on the last beat plus reaffirm, CAG -4% on a beat plus reaffirm today) and the baseline_tension caveat must reach the number, so expected_move goes from +1.0 to +0.4, visibly below the +0.8 sum.
Lesson 9: Flavor Solutions softness (flattish volume, QSR) is netted inside the one finding against Consumer improvement rather than filed as a separate negative. No change to the count.
Lesson 5: the peer data (CAG volume -2.1%) and the tariff and freight macro were kept as reaction-function context and not filed as company findings. This was already true of the draft.
